by_judge.judge: M.NAGAPRASANNA IS NOT HOLDING SITTING ON

narrative:
On July 24, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 2,190 cases across 50 judges and heard 808 matters, achieving an overall hearing rate of 36.9%. This represents a decline in judicial throughput compared to preceding days, dropping from 42.0% (1,005 of 2,392 cases) on July 23, 40.9% on July 22, and 46.6% on July 21. Both total scheduled volume and absolute cases heard reached multi-day lows.

Judicial performance varied significantly across court halls. High-performing benches included Judge T.M. Nadaf in Hall 39, who processed 19 of 21 cases (90.5%), and Shivashankar Amarannavar in Hall 20, who heard 55 of 70 scheduled matters (78.6%). V. Srishananda in Hall 21 also posted strong results, hearing 59 of 78 matters (75.6%). Conversely, Division Benches comprising the Chief Justice with K.S. Hemalekha (Hall 1) and Anu Sivaraman with Venkatesh Naik T (Hall 2) reported no hearings across 65 and 49 scheduled cases, respectively. S.G. Pandit and Pradeep Singh Yerur in Hall 5 heard only 1 of 100 scheduled cases (1.0%).

By procedural stage, Orders comprised the largest share of the docket, with 324 of 716 cases heard (45.3%). Final Hearing matters saw 129 of 401 cases heard (32.2%), marking a conversion improvement over July 23 (24.4%) and July 22 (20.1%). Among case types, Writ Petitions (WP) dominated volume with 993 scheduled and 354 heard (35.6%), down from a 42.5% hearing rate on July 23. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) sustained strong output, clearing 159 of 314 cases (50.6%), while Regular Second Appeals (RSA) achieved a 62.2% clearance rate (84 of 135 cases).
